title: Counter-Selector Wave 21: remaining-gate exhaustion and independent-review launch

gate_results.basis: Contemporaneous reporting and the official mission record independently confirm that unequal state-media access, use of government property, a large multinational observer apparatus, and the election-transition context were live issues. They do not independently establish that the candidate alone caused the reported commitments, concession, or mission outcome.

Three indicators show retrospective updating, candid self-critique, or an admitted change of mind. None supplies the complete contemporaneous sequence of contradiction, attributable model revision, changed decision or object, preserved relationship, and observable repair.

The mission and other domains supplied high reputation, formal appointment, direct access, professional staff, hundreds of observers, communications infrastructure, cooperating institutions, and experienced successor personnel. The three comparator lanes are not normalized for mandate, resources, source coverage, or outcome.

The Nicaragua transition letter has no acquired copy or recipient acknowledgment. The Law of the Sea record supports successor-capable institutional continuity but not a direct state-package receipt. Archival finding aids are routes, not handoff evidence.

Exact request packets now identify the United Nations ONUVEN series, the Library of Congress Richardson papers and Law of the Sea boxes, and the Carter Library or correct-repository referral. No email, archive request, visit, duplication order, or custodian contact was sent.

GitHub issue 597 publicly requests an artifact-bounded review from someone not involved in Waves 15–20. The request omits the identity label while warning that the history may remain inferable. Opening a request is not an external review.

tests.indicator: The Nicaragua oral history says the candidate came to view Daniel and Humberto Ortega as more responsible and responsive than expected.
missing_sequence: attributable changed decision or work object

tests.indicator: The same oral history contains candid self-critique that the candidate may have failed the United Nations team by not challenging another senior observer's press-conference dominance.
missing_sequence: criticism entering the model at the time

tests.indicator: A 1974 contemporaneous profile quotes the candidate saying he had changed his mind about requiring welfare mothers to work.
missing_sequence: identified contradiction or evidence that caused the change
contemporaneous policy or work-object revision attributable to the candidate
affected-party relationship preserved through the change

candidate_support_ledger: selection for high public reputation and credibility
formal appointment by the United Nations Secretary-General
professional ONUVEN operational staff led by Iqbal Riza
cooperation from the Supreme Electoral Council
parallel OAS and Carter observer missions
prior Cabinet, diplomatic, legal, and multilateral negotiating experience

matched_comparator_lanes.unit: ONUVEN operational chief and professional mission staff
matched_comparator_lanes.reason_not_normalized: The available public record does not allocate interventions, decision rights, resource loads, and outcomes between the personal representative and the operational chief on a common metric.

matched_comparator_lanes.unit: Organization of American States election-observer mission
matched_comparator_lanes.reason_not_normalized: The OAS mission had a different mandate, scale, chain of command, and source record; its output cannot be treated as a matched person-level comparator.
The delegation was smaller, independently organized, and operated through different access and public-attention channels.

support_adjusted_surplus.reason: No resource-normalized comparator shows valid movement materially exceeding what the candidate's authority, staff, logistics, reputation, access, and prior experience would predict.

routes_tested.object: post-concession Spanish-language letter to Daniel Ortega
Law of the Sea delegation transition

next_action: Keep issue 597 open for a genuinely independent response; acquire the exact Nicaragua, Law of the Sea, and welfare-policy records only through separately authorized custodian contact or public digitization; ingest any review or archive response as a new evidence object; and refuse CS-FT-01 until model elasticity, support normalization, direct handoff, and completed independent review are established.
